question: Along a straight utility corridor, a shutoff valve is set at mile marker $x$ and a pump station stands at mile marker $9$. The maintenance log records the valve's distance from the pump station as $2x - 6$ miles. What is the value of $x$?

distractorNotes.A: solves x - 9 = 2x - 6 and keeps x = -3 without checking it; there the left side is 12 but the right side is -12
distractorNotes.B: negates only the 2x when writing the second case, solving 9 - x = 2x + 6 to get x = 1
distractorNotes.C: drops the -6 from the right side, solving 9 - x = 2x to get x = 3

explanation:
**SAT Pattern: Absolute Value Equation**

**Choice D is correct.**

**The Fast Way (~45s):** $|x - 9| = 2x - 6$ has cases $x = -3$ and $x = 5$; only $x = 5$ keeps the recorded distance positive.

**The Full Solution:**
Step 1: Distance along a line is the absolute value of the difference in positions, so the log's reading gives $|x - 9| = 2x - 6$.
Step 2: Split into two cases. Case 1: $x - 9 = 2x - 6$, which gives $x = -3$. Case 2: $-(x - 9) = 2x - 6$, that is $9 - x = 2x - 6$, so $15 = 3x$ and $x = 5$.
Step 3: Test both candidates, because a distance is never negative. At $x = -3$ the left side is $|-3 - 9| = 12$ while the right side is $2(-3) - 6 = -12$, so that root is extraneous. At $x = 5$, $|5 - 9| = 4$ and $2(5) - 6 = 4$, so $x = 5$. $\checkmark$

**Why the wrong answers are tempting:**
* Choice A ($-3$): the case-1 root, kept without checking. It would make the recorded distance $-12$ miles.
* Choice B ($1$): comes from $9 - x = 2x + 6$, negating only the $2x$ when the whole right side was never the thing being negated.
* Choice C ($3$): comes from $9 - x = 2x$, dropping the $-6$ on the right.

**Test Day Takeaway:** A distance between two positions is an absolute value. Split it into two cases, then substitute both roots back, because a variable on the other side makes one root extraneous.
